title: Close error capture
hints: `Save` has a **named** `err` result, so a deferred closure can see what the function is about to return and change it. Defer the close only **after** `open` succeeded.

`defer func() { if cerr := s.Close(); cerr != nil && err == nil { err = fmt.Errorf("close: %w", cerr) } }()`. Because it's deferred it also runs when `Write` panics — and since it doesn't call `recover`, the panic continues afterwards.

`SaveBatches` must not `defer` inside its loop. Reuse `Save`, which closes before it returns: `if err := Save(func() (Store, error) { return open(i) }, lines); err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("batch %d: %w", i, err) }`.
